headline: EVERY PAPER ENDORSES ITS OWNER
body: The proprietor's newspapers independently reach the same conclusion, using the same photograph and the same typo.

responses.label: Acknowledge the ownership openly
responses.flavour: The disclosure is awkward. The typo becomes the bigger story.

responses.label: Celebrate the independent consensus
responses.flavour: The graduates post the ownership chart. Voss calls their chart regrettably effective.

headline: PROPRIETOR AGREES TO AN INTERVIEW SHE DOES NOT OWN
body: A broadcaster promises difficult questions. Voss considers purchasing the broadcaster, then remembers the deadline.

responses.label: Prepare straight answers
responses.flavour: The candidate gives an unexpectedly solid answer about flood defences.

responses.label: Attack the interviewer's agenda
responses.hint: An argument instead of an answer.
responses.flavour: The clip is everywhere. So is the unanswered question.

headline: CLIENT SENDS A PRE-WRITTEN DENIAL OF KNOWLEDGE
body: The document blames a hypothetical consultant for hypothetical misconduct. It already contains your actual name.

responses.label: Demand it be withdrawn
responses.hint: You have noticed the bus approaching.
responses.flavour: Voss calls you sensitive. The document disappears, but the risk of being sacrificed does not.

responses.label: Accept the nature of the relationship
responses.flavour: She promises you are invaluable. The denial remains in her drafts.

headline: WHAT DO YOU PUT IN WRITING?
body: The campaign wants a note setting out the last stretch. This one may eventually be read aloud by someone wearing a wig.

responses.label: A lawful final push
responses.flavour: The note is refreshingly dull. The field team knows what to do.

responses.label: A ruthless media offensive
responses.hint: Any criminal special remains a separate, risky choice.
responses.flavour: Voss approves your combative tone. Nobody promises to protect you.
